rv.q: Her delivery of Mr. Beane’s dialogue ensures that theatergoers who thought that wit that both sings and stings would never echo again on Broadway without a British accent have cause to rejoice.
But laughs aside, its chaotic structure, glib tone and surfeit of tangential padding underline that something is missing.
"Little Dog" takes sharp little nips at bones strewn around our cultural of hypocrisy, but never breaks any skin.
Planted firmly in the driver’s seat Julie White puts the medal to the pedal for an adrenaline spiked ride that is a laughed filled delight.
White, who originated Diane when The Little Dog Laughed first opened at Second Stage in January, is giving one of the most resplendent comic performances I've ever seen.

aw.sub: Won Best Actress in a Play

cn.t: Beane's sharp satire of Hollywood hypocrisy and closeted celebrity earns praise for its witty zingers and comedic craft, though critics split on whether its glib tone and chaotic structure undermine the substance.

vs.sum: A beautifully restored theater with a stunning Tiffany-inspired interior. The 2021 renovation transformed restroom facilities from among Broadway's worst to a model for the industry, with modern bathrooms on every public level.

acc.note: Elevator to Mezzanine, Balcony, and lower level restrooms. 7 wheelchair spaces across all levels.
